newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Jan gains on cold, charts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Jan gains on cold, charts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Tuesday in a moderate session, with technical buying and revised forecasts for colder weather later this week reversing some early January weakness, sources said.
January rallied 11.8 cents to close at $3.364 per million British thermal units after dipping to $3.11 early. February settled 13.1 cents higher at $3.017. Others ended mixed.

"Until the second week of December, we're still a captive audience to the Weather Channel. Revised forecasts (for colder weather) added to the nervousness," said one Midwest trader, noting cash and futures had nearly converged.

Mild weather early this week set a bearish tone for the early-December cash and helped pressure paper Monday. But traders agreed the market would remain vulnerable early in the winter season to volatile swings based on weather.
"For a while, we're at the whim of Mother Nature," the Midwest trader said.

Despite Monday's sharp selloff, technical traders said longer-term uptrends were still intact. They pegged January support at $3.10 and then at $3.04, a low from November 21. Resistance was seen in the remaining gap at $3.435-3.44 and then in the $3.59-3.60 area. The contract high is $3.68.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded more than 25 cents Tuesday to the $3.40 area. Midcontinent pipes fell almost 20 cents to the high-$3.30s. New York city gate gas notionally was talked down a similar amount in the $4.10-4.20 area.
The 12-month strip rose 2.9 cents to $2.441. NYMEX said 38,817 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 26,123.
NYMEX Alberta natgas was untraded Tuesday but January settled 10 cents lower at $1.60.
NYMEX Permian natgas also was untraded, with January ending down five cents at $3.00.
On the KCBT, January finished seven cents higher at $3.19, while deferreds closed one to 11 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 4.8 cents to 17.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
